questions.question: What is pocket money?
options: Money a person receives from their parents
Money a person must spend right away
Money a child receives from the bank to a children’s account
questions.explanation: Pocket money is a set amount given by parents to help children learn about value.

questions.question: Why do children receive pocket money?
options: So money is spent on their desires
So they learn to manage money
So they always have more than others
questions.explanation: It is a tool for learning how to make choices and handle a budget.

questions.question: What can happen if a child spends all their pocket money at once?
options: They will not have any money later
They can go to the bank and collect more money
questions.explanation: Money is finite; once it is spent, you must wait for the next allowance.

questions.question: What is the best way to deal with the pocket money a child receives?
options: Divide the money between now and later
questions.explanation: Splitting money ensures you can enjoy something now while saving for the future.

questions.question: Chrumko has 10 euros and knows he is going to the cinema in a few days. What should he do?
options: Put aside part of the money
questions.explanation: Saving a portion ensures he has enough for his planned cinema trip.

questions.question: Chrumko buys a small thing and keeps the rest. Why?
options: Because he had no other option
So he will have money later as well
Because he did not want to buy anything
To spend less time in the shop
questions.explanation: Keeping change allows for future purchases or emergencies.

questions.question: Is it good to spend all the money at once?
options: No, it is better to divide it
questions.explanation: Dividing money helps maintain financial security over time.

questions.question: Why do we divide our money?
options: So we have money for later as well
So we cannot enjoy life too much
So we do not have to count it
questions.explanation: It prevents running out of funds before the next income.

questions.question: What does dividing money teach us?
options: Not to think about the purchase
questions.explanation: It builds the skill of prioritizing needs over wants.

questions.question: Chrumko puts aside 7 euros from 10 euros. Why?
options: So he can buy something else later
Because he does not like shopping
questions.explanation: Saving 7 euros creates a budget for a future goal.

questions.question: Chrumko keeps part of the money and later goes for pizza that he had saved for. What does this show?
options: That the money appeared at the right time
questions.explanation: The pizza is the reward for his successful planning and saving.

questions.question: What does the decision “now vs later” mean?
options: To decide whether to spend the money now or keep it for later
To buy more things now and fewer things later
To not spend money at all
questions.explanation: It is the choice between immediate satisfaction and future benefit.

questions.question: What can happen if we keep the money for later?
options: They will double and we will have more money
We will not be able to use them until old age
questions.explanation: Saving small amounts over time adds up to a larger sum for better items.

questions.question: What does waiting with a purchase teach us?
questions.explanation: Patience is a key financial virtue that prevents impulse buying.

questions.question: Is it always good to buy the first thing we see?
options: No, it is worth thinking about it
questions.explanation: Thinking first helps you decide if you actually need the item.

questions.question: Chrumko does not buy a lollipop even though he wants it, but waits. Why?
options: He wants to buy something bigger later
questions.explanation: He is practicing delayed gratification for a bigger goal.

questions.question: After thinking, Chrumko later buys a colouring book. What does this show?
options: He decided to wait and plan his purchase.
questions.explanation: Planning allowed him to get a more lasting item than a simple sweet.

questions.question: Why is it good to plan what we will use our money for?
options: So we do not have to think
questions.explanation: Planning reduces waste and ensures money goes toward what matters.

questions.question: What can happen if we spend money without thinking?
options: We might run out of money later
questions.explanation: Impulse spending often leads to a lack of funds for necessities.

questions.question: What does planning help us decide?
options: How much to spend now and how much to keep
Who to go to the shop with
questions.explanation: It helps balance current needs with future desires.

questions.question: Chrumko wants ice cream and glasses. What should he do?
options: Buy ice cream and put the rest of the money aside for the glasses
Buy only one thing without thinking
Buy two scoops of ice cream and then a whole box of other ice cream to take home
questions.explanation: This compromise satisfies a current craving while progressing toward a goal.

questions.question: Chrumko puts aside all his money even though he felt like having ice cream and a week later he could buy glasses. What does this mean?
options: He did not think about what he would do with his money
He suppressed his short‑term desire for ice cream so he could save sooner for what he needed
He made a foolish decision because he ignored his craving for ice cream even though he could have bought it
questions.explanation: Prioritizing needs over immediate wants helps achieve goals faster.

questions.question: Is it normal to make a mistake when spending money?
questions.explanation: Everyone makes mistakes; the important part is learning from them.

questions.question: What do financial mistakes help us learn?
options: How to get rid of money faster
questions.explanation: Mistakes show us the consequences of poor planning.

questions.question: What should we do after we make a mistake?
options: Notice it and think about what we can do differently next time
Ignore it, because if we do not notice it, it did not happen
Give up and never buy anything again
questions.explanation: Reflection is how we improve our money management skills.

questions.question: Why do things we buy without thinking often make us regret later?
options: Because we do not value them
questions.explanation: Regret usually comes from realizing the money could have been used better.

questions.question: Chrumko buys something he later does not use. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: Buying unused items is a waste of resources.

questions.question: What should Chrumko do next time if he makes a financial mistake?
options: Repeat it again to make sure
questions.explanation: Slowing down and thinking prevents repeating the same mistake.
